entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 76:1-12 . On Neginoth --(See on Ps 4:1 , title). This Psalm commemorates what the preceding anticipates: God's deliverance of His people by a signal interposition of power against their enemies. The occasion was probably the events narrated in 2Ki 19:35; Isa 37:1-28 . (Compare Ps 46:1-11 ).

entries.heading: 3. brake . . . the arrows
entries.text: 3. brake . . . the arrows --literally, "thunderbolts" ( Ps 78:48 ), from their rapid flight or ignition (compare Ps 18:14; Eph 6:16 ). the battle --for arms ( Ho 2:18 ).

entries.heading: 4. Thou
entries.text: 4. Thou --God. mountains of prey --great victorious nations, as Assyria ( Isa 41:15; Eze 38:11, 12; Zec 4:7 ).

entries.heading: 5. slept their sleep
entries.text: 5. slept their sleep --died ( Ps 13:3 ). none . . . found . . . hands --are powerless.

entries.heading: 6. chariot and horse
entries.text: 6. chariot and horse --for those fighting on them (compare Ps 68:17 ).

entries.heading: 7. may . . . sight
entries.text: 7. may . . . sight --contend with Thee ( De 9:4; Jos 7:12 ).
8, 9. God's judgment on the wicked is His people's deliverance ( Ps 9:12; 10:7 ).
10. Man's wrath praises God by its futility before His power. restrain --or, "gird"; that is, Thyself, as with a sword, with which to destroy, or as an ornament to Thy praise.
11, 12. Invite homage to such a God ( 2Ch 32:23 ), who can stop the breath of kings and princes when He wills ( Da 5:23 ).
